column1: # Known-broken T-SQL blocks in Markdown -- read by scripts/lint-tsql.ps1 -Baseline.
#   hash  first 12 hex digits of SHA-256 over the block's text (LF line endings)
# Every line here is a real or suspected defect in a documented recipe: SQL a
# reader would copy that SQL Server's own parser rejects. They are listed rather
# than fixed in the change that introduced the gate because each fix changes a
# technical claim, and CLAUDE.md requires each claim to be validated against
# Microsoft Learn first. "MS Learn:" notes are already confirmed there;
# "suspected:" notes are the parser's finding plus a likely cause, not yet
# This file is meant to shrink to empty:
#   - Fixing a block changes its hash, so it drops out of this list and must
#     then parse. Delete its line in the same commit.
#   - A line whose block now parses, moved, or was deleted fails the gate as a
#     stale entry, so nothing lingers here once fixed.
#   - Do not add lines to silence a new failure. A deliberate fragment gets an
#     in-document  <!-- lint-tsql: skip <reason> -->  marker; a new defect gets
#     fixed. `lint-tsql.ps1 -EmitBaseline` prints candidate lines, but each one

column3: suspected: XE predicate uses IN; predicates are built from pred_compare operators with AND/OR/NOT -- rewrite as an OR chain
suspected: EXEC parameter value is an expression (CAST(...)); EXEC accepts only constants or variables -- assign to a variable first
suspected: ALTER DATABASE MODIFY FILE SIZE takes a literal, not a variable -- build the statement with dynamic SQL
suspected: ENCRYPTION BY DATABASE MASTER KEY is not an ALTER CERTIFICATE ... WITH PRIVATE KEY option; omit ENCRYPTION BY to protect the key with the DMK
suspected: BACKUP CERTIFICATE TO FILE / PRIVATE KEY FILE given variables; verify against MS Learn, likely needs dynamic SQL
suspected: column_master_key_definition_name is not a CREATE COLUMN ENCRYPTION KEY argument; the documented argument is COLUMN_MASTER_KEY = name
missing GO: CREATE FUNCTION must be the only statement in its batch, so the CREATE SECURITY POLICY after it fails (Msg 111)
suspected: CREATE COLUMN MASTER KEY ... FROM PROVIDER = is not the documented form; it is WITH (KEY_STORE_PROVIDER_NAME = ..., KEY_PATH = ...)
suspected: SEEDING_MODE is a replica option (ALTER AVAILABILITY GROUP ... MODIFY REPLICA ... WITH (SEEDING_MODE = AUTOMATIC)), not ALTER DATABASE SET HADR
